nodes.label: Knowledge Graph Extraction
nodes.summary: Turn an arbitrary corpus (code, docs, papers, images, video) into a clustered knowledge graph with community detection, plus HTML/JSON/report outputs. Implemented by the graphify skill.

nodes.label: Confidence-Tagged Edges (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS)
nodes.summary: Every asserted relationship carries a provenance tag and numeric confidence so invented links are distinguishable from evidenced ones. Never invent an edge; use AMBIGUOUS when unsure.

nodes.label: Parallel Subagent Fan-Out
nodes.summary: Split a large file corpus into chunks and dispatch all extraction subagents in a single message so they run concurrently; sequential dispatch defeats the purpose. Requires write-capable general-purpose agents.

nodes.label: Read-Only Subagent Silently Drops Results
nodes.summary: Dispatching extraction subagents as the read-only Explore type means they cannot write chunk files, so results vanish with no error. Detected by checking chunk files exist on disk.

nodes.label: Incremental Re-Extraction with Cache
nodes.summary: Hash-based manifest plus a semantic cache means only new or changed files are re-extracted; code-only changes skip the LLM path entirely and run AST extraction alone.

nodes.label: Graph Artifacts (HTML, JSON, report, vault, Neo4j)
nodes.summary: graphify emits graph.html, graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, and optionally an Obsidian vault, wiki, SVG, GraphML, and Cypher/Neo4j push.

nodes.label: MCP Server Integration
nodes.summary: Configure and connect external services to Claude Code via Model Context Protocol servers declared in .mcp.json or plugin.json, exposing their tools to commands and agents.

nodes.label: MCP Transport Selection (stdio/SSE/HTTP/ws)
nodes.summary: Four transports with different tradeoffs: stdio for local/custom servers, SSE for hosted OAuth services, HTTP for stateless token APIs, WebSocket for real-time bidirectional streams.

nodes.label: Credentials via Environment Variables, Never Hardcoded
nodes.summary: Tokens and keys are injected through ${VAR} expansion and documented in the README; hardcoding or committing credentials is forbidden, and OAuth is preferred where the service supports it.

nodes.label: Least-Privilege Tool Allowlisting
nodes.summary: Pre-allow only the specific MCP tools a command needs rather than wildcarding a whole server; skills declare narrow allowed-tools lists for the same reason.

nodes.label: Batch and Parallelize Tool Calls
nodes.summary: Prefer one filtered query over N individual lookups, cache expensive results, and issue independent calls in parallel rather than serially.

nodes.label: Root Cause Before Any Fix
nodes.summary: The Iron Law of systematic debugging: no fixes without root cause investigation first. Symptom fixes count as failure, and the four-phase process is mandatory even under time pressure.

nodes.label: Four-Phase Debugging Workflow
nodes.summary: Investigation, then pattern analysis, then single-hypothesis testing, then implementation with a failing test. Each phase must complete before the next.

nodes.label: Backward Call-Stack Tracing
nodes.summary: Trace a bug backward from where it surfaces through each caller until the original trigger is found, adding stack-trace instrumentation when manual tracing stalls, then fix at the source.

nodes.label: Component-Boundary Instrumentation
nodes.summary: In multi-component systems, log what enters and exits each boundary once to gather evidence of WHERE the failure is before proposing any fix.

nodes.label: Defense-in-Depth Validation
nodes.summary: After finding a root cause, validate at every layer the data passes through (entry, business logic, environment guard, debug logging) so the bug becomes structurally impossible.

nodes.label: Condition-Based Waiting
nodes.summary: Replace arbitrary sleeps and timeouts in tests with polling on the actual condition, with a bounded timeout and a clear error, eliminating load-dependent flakiness.

nodes.label: Arbitrary Timeouts Cause Flaky Tests
nodes.summary: Guessing at timing with setTimeout/sleep creates race conditions that pass locally and fail under CI load; escalating the sleep value is the classic thrashing pattern.

nodes.label: Three Failed Fixes Means Wrong Architecture
nodes.summary: When three fixes fail and each reveals a new problem elsewhere, the pattern itself is wrong; stop fixing and escalate to an architectural discussion with the human.

nodes.label: Pressure-Resistant Rule Language
nodes.summary: Skills are bulletproofed with ALWAYS/NEVER phrasing, an explicit Iron Law, redundant restatement, and a rationalizations table naming the exact shortcut that feels justified in the moment.

nodes.label: Subagent Pressure Testing of Skills
nodes.summary: Validate a process skill by running scripted scenarios at a subagent: an academic no-pressure comprehension test plus emergency, sunk-cost/exhaustion, and authority/social-pressure scenarios that tempt the shortcut.

nodes.label: Failing Test First (TDD)
nodes.summary: No production code without a failing test first; the test must be watched failing for the right reason, then minimal code written to pass. Code written before its test is deleted.

nodes.label: Vertical Slice Iteration
nodes.summary: One test then one implementation, repeated, rather than writing all tests then all code. Horizontal slicing produces tests of imagined shape rather than actual behavior.

nodes.label: Adversarial Review Before Shipping
nodes.summary: Work is checked by a fresh, differently-scoped reviewer before it cascades: a code-reviewer subagent given curated context rather than session history, returning severity-ranked findings and a verdict.

nodes.label: Curated Context, Not Session History
nodes.summary: Delegated agents receive a precisely built prompt (description, requirements, git SHA range) instead of the parent's conversation, keeping the reviewer on the work product and preserving the parent's context.

nodes.label: Severity-Calibrated Findings
nodes.summary: Review output is structured as Strengths, then Critical / Important / Minor issues with file:line and why-it-matters, then a clear ready-to-merge verdict. Not everything is Critical.

nodes.label: Read-Only Review Isolation
nodes.summary: A reviewing agent must not mutate the working tree, index, HEAD, or branches; inspect via git show/diff/log and use a separate worktree if another revision is needed.

nodes.label: Minimal Solution Ladder (YAGNI)
nodes.summary: Climb rungs and stop at the first that holds: does it need to exist, does the codebase already have it, stdlib, native platform, installed dependency, one line, then minimum code. Deletion over addition.

nodes.label: Comprehension Before Simplification
nodes.summary: Laziness shortens the solution, never the reading: trace the full flow and every caller first. A small diff in the wrong place is a confident wrong fix, and the lazy fix IS the root-cause fix.

nodes.label: Context Handoff Before Reset
nodes.summary: Produce a structured summary so a fresh agent resumes seamlessly: decisions, shipped changes, key absolute paths, running state, verified-vs-assumed claims, deferrals, and one pick-up-here line.

nodes.label: Chat-Only Output, Writes Nothing
nodes.summary: session-handoff deliberately writes no file and touches no memory; persistence to the ledgers is a separate skill's job. This is the boundary that distinguishes it from wrapup.

nodes.label: Separate Verified State from Assumed State
nodes.summary: Every claim about live systems is either checked this session (say how, stamp the real time) or explicitly marked NOT re-verified. Stale belief presented as current forces the next session to re-derive everything.

nodes.label: Open Questions Are Obligations
nodes.summary: Anything left OPEN in a handoff must be resolved or re-asked before the next session starts new work, because requirements have been silently re-typed and promised artifacts lost across resets.

nodes.label: Transcript Export with Paste-Ready Handoff Prompt
nodes.summary: Save the whole conversation verbatim to a dated markdown file under handoffs/, with summary, decisions, open threads, and a fenced paste-ready prompt to resume in a new chat.

nodes.label: Ledger Persistence at Session End
nodes.summary: wrapup closes a session by striking finished tasks with a date in the task ledger, rewriting the hot cache, and appending a dated newest-first log entry so work is never re-run.

nodes.label: Propose and Confirm Before Writing Done
nodes.summary: wrapup shows a proposed Done/Now/Next split and waits for a one-line approval before touching files; a wrong Done is the exact failure the gate exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Paste-Box Prompt as the Deliverable
nodes.summary: The actual handoff to another executor is a single fenced code block with no surrounding prose inside it, short and imperative, so it copies in one click.

nodes.label: Read Current Code and Docs Before Briefing
nodes.summary: Never write recommendations from memory: read the actual repo files and existing vault docs, archive superseded briefs, and cross-reference screenshots against the rendering component before proposing fixes.

nodes.label: No Fabricated Domain Content
nodes.summary: Joshua authors the LSAT curriculum; the agent never invents content. Suspected fabrications from prior runs are flagged to a content-audit file rather than silently rewritten, and sources are verified verbatim or from git history.

nodes.label: Joshua's Voice Constraints
nodes.summary: No em dashes anywhere, terse and opinionated rather than hedged, no AI-slop vocabulary, 'modules'/'steps' never 'phases', and push back when a direction adds complexity.

nodes.label: Route to the Direct Path Before Delegating
nodes.summary: Only hand a task to the Lovable UI when it is genuinely gated there; schema changes go through Supabase migration tools and code changes are made and pushed directly.

nodes.label: Browser-Driven Platform Automation
nodes.summary: Drive a logged-in Chrome session against a third-party SPA to perform a multi-step workflow end to end (LSAT Lab set creation), capturing IDs and URLs as it goes.

nodes.label: Verification Gates Between Steps
nodes.summary: Each risky step ends in a named GATE with an expected numeric check and a listed recovery; never proceed past a failed gate. Autonomy continues only while gates pass.

nodes.label: Verify by Reading Data, Not by Eyeballing
nodes.summary: For anything beyond a handful of rows, run a JS snippet that returns compact structured counts and ordering assertions rather than trusting a screenshot, and identify records by stable ID not row position.

nodes.label: Stale Coordinates and Re-Render Races
nodes.summary: A re-rendering SPA shifts layout between actions, so reused click coordinates silently select nothing or open the wrong record; screenshot before every click and open by ID.

nodes.label: Shared Append-Only Run Ledger
nodes.summary: Each run appends a structured per-item entry (counts, IDs, URLs, date) to a log file that sibling skills read to locate prior work and append their own status lines. Fields are never removed or reformatted.

nodes.label: Explicit Sibling-Skill Scope Boundary
nodes.summary: Skills that could be confused with each other state the disambiguation table up front and hand off rather than overreach, e.g. mega-set vs set-builder vs transcribe, or the Higgsfield family's NOT-for lists.

nodes.label: Premium Design Upgrade Audit
nodes.summary: Scan an existing project, diagnose generic AI design fingerprints (Inter everywhere, purple gradients, three equal cards, Lucide icons), and apply targeted fixes in a risk-ordered sequence without changing the stack.

nodes.label: Work Within the Existing Stack
nodes.summary: Improve what is there rather than rewriting: no framework or styling-library migration, no breaking functionality, check dependencies before importing, keep changes small and reviewable.

nodes.label: Generative Media Creation
nodes.summary: Submit image, video, 3D, and audio generation jobs through the Higgsfield CLI, including marketplace listing card sets whose compliance templates live server-side.

nodes.label: CLI Bootstrap and Auth Precheck
nodes.summary: Before any command, install the CLI if it is missing from PATH and stop to ask the user to re-authenticate interactively if the session is expired.

nodes.label: Messaging Channel Access Control
nodes.summary: Manage who can reach the agent over a messaging channel by editing a JSON allowlist/policy/pending-pairing file that the channel server re-reads; covers iMessage and Discord.

nodes.label: Untrusted Channel Input / Prompt Injection
nodes.summary: Messages arriving over a channel can carry prompt injection, so access mutations must never be downstream of them. Auto-approving 'the one pending pairing' is exactly what an injected request looks like.

nodes.label: Read-Before-Write on Shared State Files
nodes.summary: Always re-read a JSON state file immediately before writing it, because a concurrent server process may have added entries; pretty-print so it stays hand-editable.

nodes.label: Skill Catalog Installation
nodes.summary: List and install skills from a curated GitHub catalog or an arbitrary repo path into the runtime's skills directory, with download-then-git-sparse-checkout fallback and abort-if-exists.

nodes.label: Hook-Based Dangerous Command Blocking
nodes.summary: A PreToolUse hook intercepts Bash calls and blocks destructive git commands (push, reset --hard, clean -f, branch -D, checkout .) before execution, exiting non-zero with a BLOCKED message.

nodes.label: Safety Enforced at the Tool Layer
nodes.summary: Dangerous capability is constrained by harness configuration (hooks, allowed-tools, permission lists) rather than by asking the model to behave, so the guardrail holds regardless of prompt content.

nodes.label: Google Workspace Access via gws CLI
nodes.summary: Workspace surfaces (Slides, Chat, Events subscriptions) are reached through the gws binary; every generated skill points at a shared gws-shared skill for auth, global flags, and security rules.

nodes.label: Inspect Schema Before Calling an API Method
nodes.summary: Run the CLI's schema/help subcommand to learn a method's required params, types, and defaults before constructing the call, rather than guessing flags.

nodes.label: Confirm Before Any Outbound Write Action
nodes.summary: Commands that send or mutate on an external system are flagged as write operations requiring explicit user confirmation before execution.

nodes.label: Subscription Expiry and Renewal
nodes.summary: Workspace Events subscriptions silently expire unless renewed within a window; the remedy is a scheduled bulk renew across everything expiring soon.

nodes.label: Interactive Field Supplementation
nodes.summary: Locate an existing research outline file, source candidate new fields from the user or a web-search agent, display them for confirmation, then append in place.

nodes.label: User Confirmation Gate Before Mutation
nodes.summary: A shared pattern where the agent proposes a concrete change set and blocks on an explicit human yes before writing, used for ledgers, research fields, generation runs, and access changes.
